summary: Prepared six hash-disjoint geometry-only held-out TS validation candidates spanning rising, near-saddle, and falling regions; no VASP or GPU job was submitted.

payload.objective: Establish whether the current AQCat25 checkpoint can be calibrated for the Fe(110) hydrogen-transfer TS/path domain before using it to accelerate the remaining C* + H* -> CH* transition-state search.
current_evidence: Six geometry-only held-out candidates were prepared: two rising-path, two near-saddle, and two falling-path structures.
All six retain 47 atoms, the endpoint cell and atom order, PBC, Selective Dynamics, and the bottom 18 Fe atoms exactly fixed.
All six exact file hashes and validator-rounded geometry fingerprints are disjoint from the 18 active-training and adsorption-replay structures and from current source path images 00-08.
C-H coverage is 2.538, 2.194, 1.723, 1.293, 1.123, and 1.092 A; minimum pair distance across the set is 1.092 A.
A separate dense segmented-IDPP attempt was rejected because its C-H coordinate backtracked 1.70 -> 3.58 -> 1.11 A.
These are unevaluated candidate geometries only. No VASP label, AQCat25 prediction, TS-domain calibration, scientific TS validation, or reportable energy exists for them.
payload.one_executable_step: Obtain user geometry approval for at least five of the six frozen candidates; do not prepare or submit VASP/GPU validation jobs without explicit authorization.
payload.submission_boundary: No VASP force-label submission, GPU prediction, fine-tuning, ML-NEB rerun, NEB, DIMER, frequency, connectivity, or barrier action is authorized by candidate preparation.
done_when: At least five disjoint held-out VASP-labeled TS-domain structures pass registered bootstrap calibration metrics for the exact checkpoint and compatibility branch.
A hash-bound calibration review decides whether this checkpoint is reusable for the in-scope hydrogen-transfer path domain.
Only after calibration may the strategy engine choose the least-cost VASP NEB/CI-NEB/DIMER continuation from the complete path evidence.
